clauses.reason: The complete order explicitly terminates the specified stay: "do hereby order ... be terminated." It states no delayed effective date, future act, notice requirement or unresolved condition for this termination. Its own White House date and matched APP metadata support September 14, 1934. The prior emergency-trigger conditions describe the stay being removed; they are not prerequisites newly imposed on this termination. The completed dispositive act cannot first cease before it is made. Later Schechter/repeal events concern the resulting code regime, not performance of this command. All three whereas paragraphs supply factual/background reasons. The sole operative paragraph performs unconditional termination and states its boundary. It assigns no future report, appointment, investigation, payment or repeat action. Exhaustion follows the express self-executing disposition, not signature alone.

research_rationale:
The frozen shared brief supplies conditional source propositions only. NIRA section 3 code authority, Schechter (May 27, 1935), and S.J.Res.113 (June 14, 1935) are not assigned automatically as first endpoints; the latter repeals code approval/enforcement and separately extends remaining Title I. EO7076 and EO7252 defeat categorical extinction of all administration. The unnamed-instruments and strike/insert rulings remain applicable. Original replacement and quotation recheck remain required. The complete order explicitly terminates the specified stay: "do hereby order ... be terminated." It states no delayed effective date, future act, notice requirement or unresolved condition for this termination. Its own White House date and matched APP metadata support September 14, 1934. The prior emergency-trigger conditions describe the stay being removed; they are not prerequisites newly imposed on this termination. The completed dispositive act cannot first cease before it is made. Later Schechter/repeal events concern the resulting code regime, not performance of this command. Only section 1 of Article IX is released. The operative paragraph also expressly preserves the rest of the June 9 approval. The saving sentence limits the scope of this termination; it does not direct a new officer, require a new performance or create an additional code. Full EO6734A confirms the parent conditions. This is express termination, not strike-and-insert wording replacement.

This proposal does not approve the parent's full lifecycle, assert ongoing code validity through 2026, or extinguish accrued rights by inference.
